judgements.justification: Each committee had one wrong claim (A: FpoL's 'never justified', aGgD's 'without captions'; B: YyKC on Meinke and Hein), and none lowered a score or drove the tier gap.
A's AC made four 7s a spotlight although no reviewer rated above 7 or argued for a highlight, and two doubted significance or adoption; the meta-review cites only consensus.
A's Reviewer_aGgD gave 7 at confidence 1 after 'a cursory glance', praising Fig. 6, and that score counted toward the unanimous slate behind the spotlight.
The authors admitted the CIFAR-10-C loader bug that color-inverted the Fig. 6 data only on B's forum; A judged the buggy figure without knowing it.
B learned of the loader bug, yet its meta-review omits it and calls the paper 'practically sound', and oTxs and YyKC raised on the rerun.
The rebuttal raised scores in both committees (three in A, two in B), so it did not move one committee only.
Only B's reviewers found the CIFAR-10-C bug, the weak Deep Ensemble baseline, and the ablation showing a quadratic kernel nearly matches DSCS.
Both committees noted last-layer Laplace as the only main-text base BNN; A's reviewer still raised to 7, while B's AC named it a remaining concern at poster.
Neither panel was split; B's AC summarised the open points of two reviewers rather than adopting one reviewer to settle a split.
No score moved because of other reviewers' reviews; every raise followed the authors' replies.
No reviewer's score was held down by a misread or unanswered question; the authors answered each follow-up.
A's aGgD posted a confidence-1, 1.5-hour review and replied only 'I keep my score', and that 7 counted unchallenged in A's unanimity.
Neither AC went below its reviewers' ratings; both accepted.
Neither AC decided by an average-score threshold against its own view.
No reviewer held a below-threshold score.
Both committees judged the paper as the same methodological contribution with theory and experiments.
A's raises followed added baselines and promised error terms, but no raising reviewer said the technical core was outside their expertise.
Both committees asked the same kind of questions of the paper; neither imposed an extra requirement for its type.
aGgD's praise of Fig. 6 described the figure accurately; the error lay in the authors' data, not in a wrong claim by the reviewer.
B's 4z2v kept 6 because the motivation concern stayed open, not after conceding it was resolved, and 6 is not below threshold.
A credited promised error analysis, but B did not refuse promised items; both committees accepted the paper on its rebuttal material.
Every reviewer who stated a changed position also edited the score.
No extra reviewer was called in by either AC.
Clarity verdicts did not split by reviewer field.
Every raise came with a stated reason.
Neither AC set aside a silent low rating.
B's 8 was the only rating above 7, but B got the lower tier; both committees advocated acceptance, so no missing champion explains the gap.
No reviewer admitted partial reading at high confidence; aGgD's cursory reading came with confidence 1.
4z2v disputed the infinite-ReLU framing and kernel motivation within the same tradition, not from a different theoretical school.
A's two-sentence meta-review argues only that the paper is good and well-supported, and gives no reason for a spotlight.
B's YyKC checked Fig. 6 against Ovadia et al.'s published Deep Ensemble results and exposed the bug, while A's reviewers took Fig. 6 and Table 1 at face value.
B's meta-review omits the bug, but in the paper's favour, not toward the chair's lower decision.
A's doubts about significance and adoption did not cap A's tier, and B raised no narrow-audience objection.
No low-scoring misreading detractor sat in either committee.
A saw Mahalanobis and DUQ comparisons that raised two scores, and B saw the CIFAR-10-C rerun and arc-cosine ablation; neither committee saw the other's new results.
A's highest-confidence review rated 7 like the others, and B's 8 came at confidence 4 alongside another 4; expertise was not outvoted.
No objection came after the response period closed.
A's 7s and B's 6 to 8 differ little in mean, and the verbal assessments track the ratings.

reasoning: Both committees accepted, so the split is the tier. A's AC turned four 7s into a spotlight with a meta-review that gives no case for it (R02, R30). One of those 7s was a cursory, confidence-1 review that never engaged (R03, R12). B reviewed more deeply: its reviewers checked results against published baselines (R31) and drew out a data-loader bug the authors disclosed only to B (R04, R07), plus an ablation that weakened the kernel motivation. Each committee saw new results the other did not (R35), and B's AC weighed the last-layer-Laplace limitation that A shrugged off (R08) while omitting the bug (R05). The stage 1 candidates (AC upgrade, deeper review finding a bug, unresolved motivation, raises on copied baselines, generic meta-review, cursory review) all fit existing reasons on a plain reading, so none is added.
